Funes.notes: The DSP is Émilie Gillet's Plaits at firmware 1.2, vendored unchanged at eurorack/plaits; src/Funes.cpp is the Rack wrapper, running one Plaits voice per polyphonic channel. The trigger threshold is not the 0.7V the wrapper's own comment at Funes.cpp:249 gives: Funes.cpp:250 divides the jack voltage by 3 and voice.cc:99 compares the result against 0.3, so the input goes high at 0.9V, and voice.cc:108 releases it below 0.3V. The two low-pass gate jacks are read with getVoltage() at Funes.cpp:213 and Funes.cpp:215, outside the per-channel loop, so they are monophonic and apply to every voice; the maker marks this with silver jacks and says so in the manual. The model offset is sampled and held at each trigger: voice.cc:105 copies it on the rising edge, and voice.cc:113 reads it continuously only when nothing is patched to the trigger. The LEVEL input is compressed and constrained to 0..1 at voice.cc:152, and with nothing patched the accent is fixed at 0.8 and the trigger strikes the low-pass gate instead. The menu item the manual calls Open custom data editors in web browser... is spelled Open editors in web browser... in the source.

Sanguine-Aleae.notes: This is a rewrite rather than a port of Émilie Gillet's Branches: src/aleae.cpp holds the whole coin toss, with no vendored DSP behind it. The trigger threshold is 2V, which the manual does not give. The probability total is deliberately left unclamped — the source says so in a comment at aleae.cpp:100 — because the comparison against a uniform random number between 0 and 1 saturates on its own. In toggle mode the new result is the exclusive-or of the toss and the previous result, so a heads keeps the current output and a tails changes it. The two mode lamps are lit at full brightness rather than at the plugin's button-lamp level: aleae.cpp:146 and aleae.cpp:148 multiply the enum by kSanguineButtonLightValue before the comparison rather than after it, so the expression reduces to a plain true or false. That is cosmetic and changes nothing a cable can carry.

Sets the cutoff frequency of the filter; the numbered lamps report each polyphonic channel's cutoff as a colour, red at the low end and violet at the high one

Cycles the internal oscillator through off, triangle, sawtooth and square; while it runs, its wave takes the place of the input 1 signal going into the filter

Sets the level of the signal at input 2, clipping it at high settings
Shifts the cutoff frequency through its attenuverter, 5V covering the whole FREQ knob range
Shifts the resonance through its attenuverter, 5V covering the whole RESO knob range
Scales the FREQ / LVL 1 knob, 5V giving the knob's own setting; while the internal oscillator runs it sets that oscillator's pitch, one volt per octave. With nothing patched it reads 5V
Scales the LVL 2 knob, 5V giving the knob's own setting; with nothing patched it reads 5V
The signal for module channel 1; while the internal oscillator runs it phase-modulates that oscillator instead of feeding the filter
The signal for module channel 2
The two module channels summed and passed through the filter, ±5V
The two module channels summed before the filter, ±5V, or the bare internal oscillator while that runs
Note — the module is polyphonic: the channel count comes from whichever of the two audio inputs carries more, and every channel runs its own filter.
Note — the two module channels are not the polyphonic channels: each polyphonic channel has a channel 1 and a channel 2 of its own, fed by the two audio inputs or by the internal oscillator.

Note — bypassing the module passes input 1 straight to the 1 + 2 output.
Sanguine-Scalaria.notes: The filter is the low-pass ladder from the Symbiote firmware for Warps, lifted out into a module of its own; src/scalaria.cpp is the whole of it, running one filter per polyphonic channel. The maker cites the improved virtual analogue Moog ladder model of D'Angelo and Välimäki. The cutoff input is not volt-per-octave: scalaria.cpp:150 divides it by 5 and adds it to a normalised 0-to-1 cutoff, so it is a plain control voltage. The level jacks carry two normals each in effect: scalaria.cpp:148 reads the first with getNormalVoltage(5) for the gain and scalaria.cpp:170 reads the same jack again with getNormalVoltage(2) for the internal oscillator's pitch. THERE IS A BUG IN THE OUTPUT: scalaria.cpp:209 and scalaria.cpp:215 index the output frame buffer with the channel number instead of that channel's frame counter — outputFrames[currentChannel][currentChannel] where every neighbouring line writes outputFrames[currentChannel][frames[currentChannel]]. It affects the 1 + 2 output on the third and fourth channel of each group of four, so polyphonic channels 3, 4, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15 and 16 read a stale sample there. The AUX output on those channels is indexed correctly, and the block size of 60 keeps the wrong index inside the buffer, so this is a wrong sample rather than a crash. Nothing in the entry's lines depends on it, but somebody should check it against the running module.
